title: Issue with FAQ Schema Pro Displaying Incorrectly in Preview and Publish
summary: I'm currently facing an issue with the FAQ module in Schema Pro. While editing, everything appears normal, but once I preview or publish the page, the FAQ section renders incorrectly. Instead of displaying the expected layout, it shows JSON-LD code and duplicates the question and answer sections (as shown in the attached screenshot). Has anyone else encountered this problem ? If so, do you ...
offer_reason: Treat this as a direct service lead first.
subject_draft: Direct schema help for: Issue with FAQ Schema Pro Displaying Incorrectly in Preview and Publis
message_draft:
This looks like the FAQPage JSON-LD is being output in the wrong shape, or a required field is missing in the final live markup.

I’d check these first:
- Check the final live JSON-LD and confirm mainEntity exists at page level.
- Make sure each Question has acceptedAnswer.text in the final output.
- Check for duplicate schema coming from another plugin or theme.

title: EEA free listings since Sep 15: 531 product searches in DE/AT/CH/UK, and why Search Console shows −63 % while Merchant Center shows only −9 %
summary: Shop A, EEA: merchant listings in Search Console −63 %, free listings in Merchant Center −9 %, organic clicks on product pages +6.5 % Where 100 product items lead on mobile: DE 90 % comparison sites, AT 46 %, CH and UK 0 % (4 days, 531 searches) Same query, two countries: comparison-site groups in Germany, merchants with stars in Switzerland Since mid-September, product searches in Germany show a grid of comparison-site groups instead of merchant carousels. Google documented the new EEA units on Sep 8 (SEJ). Per Search Engine Roundtable (Sep 18), Google's Ads Liaison confirmed in a comment that free listings were removed in the EEA because of the DMA. Two questions: who fills the new grid, and what actually reaches a shop? Method 531 non-brand product searches by Keyword Planner volume across twelve sectors: 274 German terms for DE, AT and CH, 257 English terms for the UK. Four days (Oct 20–23), signed out, location set to the country. Mobile in all four countries, desktop in DE and UK: 6,440 result pages. Every product item in the block counted, including collapsed groups: where it leads and whether it shows stars. Before state: 2,299 archived SERP captures of the same terms, April to October. Shop data: Search Console, Merchant Center and web analytics of a shop I work with (Shop A, with permission, relative changes only). Who fills the grid (4-day averrage, arrow columns = share of all product items in the block) Country, device Searches with product block → comparison sites → Google Shopping with stars Germany, mobile 92 % 90 % 10 % 2 % Germany, desktop 53 % 87 % 13 % 4 % Austria, mobile 90 % 46 % 54 % 7 % Switzerland, mobile 95 % 0 % 100 % 73 % UK, mobile 100 % 0 % 100 % 71 % UK, desktop 100 % 0 % 100 % 71 % Directly to a shop: under 1 % everywhere. Germany usually shows six to eight groups per search, and no site dominates: Google Shopping 10.0 %, testberichte.de 6.6 %, billiger.de 6.3 %, shopping.de 5.7 %, idealo.de 5.5 %. The top 10 hold 57 % together, every other site is under 4 % (53,625 mobile product items). Before: 95–98 % of the German archive captures from April to June showed a product carousel. What Shop A sees (EEA, Sep 21–Oct 4 vs. Sep 1–14; same days in 2025 for comparison) Shop A 2026 2025 difference Search Console, "Merchant listings", search type Web −62.9 % −7.9 % −55 pp Merchant Center, free product listings −9.2 % −10.6 %* +1 pp Organic clicks on product pages (web search without merchant listings) +6.5 % −15.6 % +22 pp All clicks on product pages −4.3 % −15.0 % +11 pp All clicks from web search −3.5 % −12.6 % +9 pp Visits via comparison sites (web analytics, all countries and media) +13.3 % +4.8 % +9 pp **Merchant Center changed its counting on Aug 24 (recalculated from Jul 1); the 2025 values use the old counting. Search Console breaks on Sep 15, EEA only: outside the EEA, merchant listing clicks rose 12 %. By country −40 to −70 %, steepest in Germany. Why Search Console and Merchant Center disagree: the "Merchant listings" appearance counts web search (and Images with that search type). Merchant Center sums free listings across Search, Shopping tab, Images, Lens, YouTube and Maps. Before Sep 15, merchant listing clicks in Search Console were about a fifth of Merchant Center's free clicks. Different definitions, so one can't be converted into the other. Product pages: merchant listings were ~15 % of their web search clicks before. The organic rest rose 6.5 %, which by calculation offset ~57 % of the merchant listing decline on those pages. Oct 5–18 vs. Sep 1–14: Search Console merchant listings −60 % (2025: −5 %), Merchant Center −18 % (2025: −16 %), organic clicks on product pages −4.4 % (2025: −23.6 %). Context, not a control group: Keyword Planner Sep vs. Sep 2025 DE +2 %, AT +5 %, CH −3 %, UK +15 %. Google Trends (20 product terms, DE and UK) shows no dip. Bing clicks +1 %. Shopping ads: no step on Sep 15. Takeaways Read Search Console and Merchant Center together, per country. The Search Console drop is not your total loss. Product pages with complete Product markup (price, availability, variants) are the web search surface you still control. 90 % of product items in the German grid lead to comparison sites. Listing there costs per click: a budget question, not an SEO one. Keep srsltid on redirects (Merchant Center auto-tagging), or the free-listing channel becomes hard to measure. Limits Shop figures are one shop, not the market. The SERP measurement is the broad part. Volume-heavy non-brand queries, not a random sample of all searches. Signed-out automated retrieval can differ from what a person sees: 87 % of search/country/device combinations gave the same block result on all four days, German desktop only about half. Product pages are identified by URL pattern. Whether the same users moved from the listing to the organic result can't be separated. Two weeks before and after, plus Oct 5–18. Needs a repeat in a few months. Do you see similiar Data in your MCC | GSC ? /u/DrKJING

I’d check these first:
- Confirm the feed source Google/Pinterest is reading is the same one the store is publishing.
- Check for stale IDs, deleted variants, draft products, or cached feed data.
- Compare the feed values against one live product URL end-to-end.
